generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"

datasource db {
  provider = "sqlite"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")

model User {
  id           Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  email        String   @unique
  username     String   @unique
  passwordHash String
  bio          String?
  image        String?
  createdAt    DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt    DateTime @updatedAt

  articles  Article[]
  comments  Comment[]
  favorites Favorite[]
  following Follow[]   @relation("follower")
  followers Follow[]   @relation("followee")
}

model Follow {
  followerId Int
  followeeId Int

  follower User @relation("follower", fields: [followerId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  followee User @relation("followee", fields: [followeeId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@id([followerId, followeeId])
  @@index([followeeId])
}

model Article {
  id          Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  slug        String   @unique
  title       String
  description String
  body        String
  createdAt   DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime @updatedAt
  authorId    Int

  author    User         @relation(fields: [authorId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  tags      ArticleTag[]
  comments  Comment[]
  favorites Favorite[]

  @@index([authorId])
  @@index([createdAt])
}

model Tag {
  id   Int    @id @default(autoincrement())
  name String @unique

  articles ArticleTag[]
}

model ArticleTag {
  articleId Int

# RealWorld Backend — TypeScript / Fastify / Prisma / SQLite

A complete implementation of the [RealWorld backend specification](https://realworld-docs.netlify.app/specifications/backend/endpoints/):
JWT authentication, user profiles and following, article CRUD with tags, comments,
favorites and the personalised feed.

The official [Hurl](https://hurl.dev) API suite is vendored under `tests/hurl/`
(13 files, 154 requests) and passes in full.

## Requirements

- Node.js 20 or newer
- [Hurl](https://hurl.dev/docs/installation.html) — only needed to run the API tests

## Getting started

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

`npm run dev` creates `.env` from `.env.example` if needed, applies the Prisma
migrations to the SQLite database and starts the server with hot reload on
<http://localhost:3000>. The API is served under the `/api` prefix.

## Scripts

| Script              | Purpose                                                     |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `npm run dev`       | Migrate the database and start the server with hot reload    |
| `npm run build`     | Compile TypeScript to `dist/`                                |
| `npm start`         | Migrate the database and run the compiled server             |
| `npm run typecheck` | Type-check without emitting output                           |
| `npm run test:api`  | Run the vendored Hurl suite against a throwaway server       |

## Running the API tests

```bash
npm run test:api
```

The runner boots the server on port 3001 against a temporary SQLite database, waits
for `/health`, executes all 13 Hurl files sequentially and shuts everything down
afterwards. Pass specific files to narrow the run:

```bash
npm run test:api -- tests/hurl/articles.hurl
```

Expected output:

```
Executed files:    13
Executed requests: 154
Succeeded files:   13 (100.0%)
Failed files:      0 (0.0%)
```

## Endpoints

| Method   | Path                                  | Auth     |
| -------- | ------------------------------------- | -------- |
| `POST`   | `/api/users`                          | –        |
| `POST`   | `/api/users/login`                    | –        |
| `GET`    | `/api/user`                           | required |
| `PUT`    | `/api/user`                           | required |
| `GET`    | `/api/profiles/:username`             | optional |
| `POST`   | `/api/profiles/:username/follow`      | required |
| `DELETE` | `/api/profiles/:username/follow`      | required |
| `GET`    | `/api/articles`                       | optional |
| `GET`    | `/api/articles/feed`                  | required |
| `GET`    | `/api/articles/:slug`                 | optional |
| `POST`   | `/api/articles`                       | required |
| `PUT`    | `/api/articles/:slug`                 | required |
| `DELETE` | `/api/articles/:slug`                 | required |
| `POST`   | `/api/articles/:slug/favorite`        | required |
| `DELETE` | `/api/articles/:slug/favorite`        | required |
| `GET`    | `/api/articles/:slug/comments`        | optional |
| `POST`   | `/api/articles/:slug/comments`        | required |
| `DELETE` | `/api/articles/:slug/comments/:id`    | required |
| `GET`    | `/api/tags`                           | –        |

Authenticated requests carry an `Authorization: Token <jwt>` header (`Bearer` is
also accepted).

## Behaviour worth knowing

These details are asserted by the official test suite and are easy to get wrong:

- **Status codes.** Creating a user, an article or a comment returns `201`; deleting
  an article or comment returns `204`; a duplicate username or email returns `409`.
- **Error envelope.** Every failure responds with `{"errors": {"<field>": ["<message>"]}}`
  — for example `{"errors": {"token": ["is missing"]}}` or `{"errors": {"article": ["not found"]}}`.
- **`articlesCount`** reports how many articles match the filter overall, not how many
  fit on the requested page.
- **Nullable profile fields.** Sending `bio` or `image` as `""` normalises them to
  `null`; `username`, `email` and `password` reject both `""` and `null`.
- **Passwords** follow NIST 800-63B: at least 8 characters, no composition rules, and
  long passphrases are accepted as-is.
- **`tagList` on update** is authoritative when present (`[]` clears every tag) and
  leaves existing tags untouched when omitted; an explicit `null` is rejected with `422`.
- **List payloads omit `body`** entirely rather than returning it as `null`.
- **Authorization precedence.** Missing credentials produce `401` before any lookup,
  a missing resource produces `404`, and only then does ownership produce `403`.

## Project layout

```
prisma/schema.prisma   Data model and migrations
src/index.ts           Process entrypoint
src/server.ts          Fastify app assembly, error envelope, route registration
src/plugins/auth.ts    Token parsing and the requireAuth guard
src/lib/               Validation, presenters, password hashing, JWT, slugs
src/routes/            One module per resource
tests/hurl/            Vendored official Hurl suite
tests/openapi.yml      Vendored official OpenAPI description (reference only)
scripts/               Test runner and first-run .env bootstrap
```

## License

The vendored files under `tests/` come from the
[realworld-apps/realworld](https://github.com/realworld-apps/realworld) repository and
retain their original license.

TMPDIR_RUN="$(mktemp -d)"
DB_FILE="${TMPDIR_RUN}/test.db"

cleanup() {
  if [[ -n "${SERVER_PID:-}" ]] && kill -0 "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
    kill "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    wait "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
  rm -rf "$TMPDIR_RUN"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

# Unrelated tools also ship a `hurl` executable, and npm puts its own bin directories
# first on PATH. Pick the first candidate whose --version identifies the real Hurl.
find_hurl() {
  local candidate
  while IFS= read -r candidate; do
    if "$candidate" --version 2>/dev/null | head -1 | grep -qE '^hurl [0-9]'; then
      echo "$candidate"
      return 0
    fi
  done < <(type -a -p hurl 2>/dev/null; echo /opt/homebrew/bin/hurl; echo /usr/local/bin/hurl)
  return 1
}

HURL="$(find_hurl)" || {
  echo "hurl is not installed. See https://hurl.dev/docs/installation.html" >&2
  exit 1
}

# A server left over from an earlier run would answer the readiness check while
# pointing at a different database, so refuse to start rather than test the wrong one.
if lsof -ti:"${PORT}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "Port ${PORT} is already in use. Stop the process holding it, or set PORT." >&2
  exit 1
fi

export DATABASE_URL="file:${DB_FILE}"
export PORT
export NODE_ENV=test

echo "Preparing test database at ${DB_FILE}"
(cd "$ROOT" && npx prisma migrate deploy >/dev/null)

echo "Starting server on ${HOST}"
(cd "$ROOT" && npx tsx src/index.ts >"${TMPDIR_RUN}/server.log" 2>&1) &
SERVER_PID=$!

for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
  if curl -sf "${HOST}/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then break; fi
  if ! kill -0 "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "Server exited early:" >&2
    cat "${TMPDIR_RUN}/server.log" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  sleep 0.5
done

curl -sf "${HOST}/health" >/dev/null || {
  echo "Server did not become ready in time:" >&2
  cat "${TMPDIR_RUN}/server.log" >&2
  exit 1
}

FILES=("$@")
if [ ${#FILES[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
  FILES=("$ROOT"/tests/hurl/*.hurl)
fi

echo "Running Hurl tests against ${HOST} with uid=${UID_VAL} (${HURL})"
if ! "$HURL" --test --jobs 1 --variable "host=${HOST}" --variable "uid=${UID_VAL}" "${FILES[@]}"; then
  echo "--- server log ---" >&2
  tail -50 "${TMPDIR_RUN}/server.log" >&2
  exit 1
fi
